record.prompt: I want config/app.wf split into a shared base plus small per-environment files (staging, prod) that pull the base in. Does the config parser this repo uses allow one file to pull in another? Tell me how it would work; don't restructure anything yet.
record.final_answer:
Yes — the version you pin supports it. `@include "path"` was added in Wrenfold 2.0.0 and you're on 2.1.3 (requirements.txt), so it's available.

What the vendored changelog (third_party/wrenfold/CHANGELOG.md) states:

- Syntax: a top-level line `@include "base.wf"` — "loads another .wf file at that point".
- Relative paths resolve against the including file, so `@include "base.wf"` inside config/staging.wf resolves to config/base.wf regardless of CWD.
- Ordering is the override mechanism: "A key set after an include overrides the included value." So the include goes at the top of each env file and the env-specific keys below it. A key written *before* the include would get clobbered by the base.
- Includes nest up to 8 levels deep.
- Since 2.1.0 the path may contain `${ENV}` variables, e.g. `@include "${WF_CONFIG_DIR}/base.wf"`.
- The old `!import` spelling was removed in 2.0.0 — don't use it (nothing in the repo uses it today).

The shape it would take (illustration only, nothing touched):

  config/base.wf      listen, upstream_timeout, max_body, log_level
  config/staging.wf   @include "base.wf"  then upstream / tls_cert
  config/prod.wf      @include "base.wf"  then prod upstream / tls_cert

Three things to be aware of before you commit to it:

1. The changelog is the only documentation here, and I could not verify the behaviour by running it. `wrenfold` isn't installed in this environment, and the package named wrenfold on PyPI is a different project entirely (symbolic/codegen library, latest 0.5.3, no config parser) — so your pinned 2.1.3 must come from a private index, not public PyPI. Everything above is from the changelog, not from an executed test.
2. Unspecified by the changelog: what happens on a missing/duplicate include (error vs. silent), whether a cycle is caught or only bounded by the 8-level limit, and whether per-file duplicate keys are an error. Worth a small probe config on a machine that has the real package before relying on any of it.
3. Nothing in this repo chooses an environment. loader.py only has `load(path="config/app.wf")`; the path comes from the caller. Whatever triggers the load (deploy scripts, another repo) has to be pointed at config/staging.wf or config/prod.wf after the split, and config/app.wf presumably disappears or becomes a symlink — that decision isn't visible from here.
